Apple TV's 30-Episode Space Opera Masterpiece Is An S-Tier Sci-Fi Series

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Space may be infinite, but truly incredible space operas are anything but.
  • Loosely based on Isaac Asimov's book series of the same name, Apple TV's Foundation is not another run-of-the-mill, bottom-tier sci-fi show.
  • Industry observers note that foundation season 1 earned a mixed reception from viewers and critics, with many calling out its extreme creative liberties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Space may be infinite, but truly incredible space operas are anything but. For there are thousands of galaxies and parallel worlds in the sci-fi genre, but only a few are worth getting lost in. There lies the magic of one of Apple TV's greatest sci-fi highlights. It immerses viewers in a space opera so grand and scintillating that it is almost impossible not to be in complete awe.

Loosely based on Isaac Asimov's book series of the same name, Apple TV's Foundation is not another run-of-the-mill, bottom-tier sci-fi show. Its sheer brilliance lies in its ability to significantly drift away from its source material. And, yet, somehow retain the essence of Asimov's scale and themes. Unlike most epic sci-fi reveals, Foundation initially stumbled and struggled to find its feet.

Industry observers note that foundation season 1 earned a mixed reception from viewers and critics, with many calling out its extreme creative liberties. However, just when it looked like the Apple TV series would turn into another forgotten sci-fi adaptation, it leveled up like a caterpillar discovering its wings. Although still a little divisive among book readers, Foundation is undoubtedly an S-tier sci-fi series.

Instead of delivering a direct page-to-page translation of Asimov's books, Apple TV's Foundation uses the original sprawling universe as, quite literally, its "foundation." Since "the beginning of wisdom is the definition of terms," Foundation arms itself with the Socratic method and borrows some of the core concepts from the source material, including psychohistory.

Then, it ingeniously takes a detour and adds a lot of original lore to the mix. One of the biggest challenges with adapting Isaac Asimov's stories was that they span across centuries. The Apple TV series does not completely abandon the original long-term storytelling. However, it also refuses to change its main characters every few chapters like the books.

Industry observers note that the show seems to understand that, in audiovisual storytelling, viewers need long-term rootable characters. A narrative cannot merely survive on abstract ideas, mathematical predictions, history, and constantly shifting perspectives. Owing to this, Apple TV's Foundation introduced everything from cloning to digital consciousness to be able to have more long-running character arcs.

Recent findings suggest that it must be noted, though, that the Apple TV sci-fi show is not the best adaptation. In 3 seasons, so far, it has drifted far enough from the books to be seen as its own thing. While there are still some overlaps between Asimov's novels and the TV series, the show is better off being treated as an original and S-tier addition to sci-fi in its own right.

One of Foundation's biggest strengths is its epic visual flair. Like most sci-fi shows on Apple TV, Foundation does not look like it is bogged down by limited small-screen budgets. Even some of the most abstract ideas from the original books are captured with such brilliant tangibility in the series that it is hard not to forgive it for its creative liberties.

From the colossal Star Bridge collapsing onto Trantor to the brutalist geometry of "The Vault" on Terminus, every frame is stunning with immense attention to detail and realism.

When these visuals are paired with Bear McCreary’s compositions, Apple TV's Foundation almost feels as grand and mythic as movies like Dune and Interstellar. It can still be debated whether the sci-fi space opera should have taken such a massive leap with its creative liberties. After all, an "adaptation" is only as good as its ability to "adapt.".

It has been revealed that but perhaps that is exactly where the real genius of the Apple TV sci-fi series lies. It does not merely change its source material to dumb down its story for the screen. Despite the changes, it is still an intelligent space opera that understands that fresh ideas and worlds are waiting to be born out of Isaac Asimov's brilliant literary works.

Industry observers note that isaac Asimov's novel series is brought to life in Foundation, a television adaptation of the epic sci-fi saga created for Apple TV+. The show follows a group of exiled humans that find themselves as the last chance to save the Galactic Empire, primarily from itself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save substantial on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Recent findings suggest that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a upcoming model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

It has been revealed that if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

Sources indicate that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, right now marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

In a recent development, if you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (presently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

Sources indicate that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

It has been revealed that no. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

Before Robert Downey Jr. spent more than a decade saving the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Iron Man, he was busy reinventing another rather famous character. Bare knuckle brawling, intrepid investigating, slow motion violence, wit, women, wonder — Downey brought it all to the table.

Industry observers note that guy Ritchie's Sherlock Holmes movies turned Arthur Conan Doyle's legendary detective into an action hero who could solve a murder and beat up half the room without breaking a sweat. The first movie was a hit, and its sequel went even bigger, sending Holmes and Watson across Europe to face their most dangerous enemy yet. There is a new criminal mastermind at large, Professor Moriarty, and not only is he Holmes' intellectual equal, but his capacity for evil, coupled with a complete lack of conscience, may actually give him an advantage over the renowned detective. Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, presently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and people who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Industry observers note that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

Recent findings suggest that it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple notes the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

In a recent development, the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

Recent findings suggest that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Sources indicate that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Industry observers note that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, at the moment the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.
  • This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….
  • Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was debuted the same month, with the company describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, at the moment the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was debuted the same month, with the company describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Muse initially debuted as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It quickly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

It has been revealed that it wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I noted at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

It has been revealed that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee noted in her post.

The report indicates this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

“I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Upgrade: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

"AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

Recent findings suggest that the instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

Meta has taken matter with the messaging claims. It states that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

With Android, users have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The company also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

The 2010s seemed like the golden age of crime dramas, with highlights like Boardwalk Empire starring Steve Buscemi, Narcos, Ozark, and Netflix's hit crime series, Peaky Blinders, starring Cillian Murphy, among several bingeworthy treats on offer. Thankfully, the 2020s have not disappointed. While the legacy of Tommy Shelby lives on beyond the events of Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man in its upcoming sequel series. Other organized crime dramas have since come on the scene. Gangs of London, Paramount+'s two-pronged delight in Tulsa King and MobLand are some of the sub-genre's more glittering additions in recent years.

Recent findings suggest that in the age of the streaming wars, Netflix's response to Paramount+'s British-laden MobLand is yet another English-centric crime drama, The Gentlemen. The hugely ambitious producer, creator, and filmmaker, Guy Ritchie, is the firm bond that links both highlights together, as Ritchie serves in several capacities behind the scenes for both productions. The second season of the Netflix series recently wrapped, signaling the initiation of production on Season 3, which is already underway. As is to be expected, several new cast additions and departures will be associated with the new chapter, even as its main stars, Theo James as the central crime boss, Edward "Eddie" Horniman, and Kaya Scodelario as Eddie's partner and associate, Sussie Glass.

According to recent reports, the reception for the first two seasons of The Gentlemen has been widely positive by critics, with Netflix also enjoying viewership success. Hence, sights have turned to Season 3 and what it might bring. Speaking during a Q&A for Netflix's The Gentlemen Season 2 FYC screening earlier this month, executive producer Matthew Read and the show's cast teased some exciting story directions for Season 3. First off, Eddie and Susie are expanding the criminal empire into the Middle East, and it's a move Read describes as being "an ascension for Eddie and Susie to become bigger than ever" with Theo James drawing comparisons with Martin Scorsese and Robert De Niro's 1995 film Casino. "[Season 3] about expansion. It's about opening the first casino in the Middle East," Read explained to the attendance. "It's like Las Vegas, and that will involve lots of million-dollar deals. And there will be lots of people competing for the rights to run this casino. So it's a sort of elevation, and it's about ascension for Eddie and Susie to become bigger than ever." To all that, James adds, "If season 2 was The Godfather Part II, this is Casino.".

By the time the season finale of The Gentlemen Season 2 aired, it became clear that James' character, Edward Horniman, had fully embraced the darkness and his position within it as a mob boss in the criminal underworld. With the Italian mafia behind him, Eddie turns his sights to the Middle East and perhaps some of the contacts he secured during the Falcon mystery in Season 2 might begin to pay off. Heading forward into Season 3, his complicated relationship with Susie, and now this news of competition for control over the casino, sets the stage for yet another colossal tussle.

Filming for The Gentlemen Season 3 has production taking place in Morocco, presumably the set for the Middle East expansion, and more recently, around London. Alongside James and Scodelario, new faces will be arriving this coming season, including Orlando Bloom, Robert Carlyle, Elijah Wood, Ed Speleers, Bugzy Malone, Saffron Burrows, Bruna Marquezine, and Dexter Fletcher.

  • Canva today announced newly introduced controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing fresh settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today announced newly introduced controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company says that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between owners with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two newly introduced controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the company noted that select features that use AI without generating new content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

“Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the company’s design content library, Canva noted that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

To learn more about today’s announcement, follow this link.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dungeon Crawler Carl is arguably one of the most successful modern science fantasy IPs in recent memory, with author Matt Dinniman's universe growing to eight massive novels since its humble beginnings as a self-published project on Royal Road. Dinniman has always had a relatively unique and unconventional approach to storytelling, but one that has captivated readers more and more with each fresh installment.

Dungeon Crawler Carl's world-building, character backstories, and unexpected array of enemies, allies, and aliens are just the beginning of what makes the story so special. One of the most interesting aspects of how the story has evolved over its lifetime is that many of the most unique and outlandish details aren't even created by Dinniman alone. The author actually breaks a longstanding "unwritten rule" among fantasy/sci-fi writers, and it's safe to say that the creative choice has paid off time and time again.

Industry observers note that these aren't just simple polls about favorite characters or potential storylines, and Dinniman gives readers different possibilities for everything from enemies and rewards to locations, names, and other unexpected details. Some of these decisions are relatively minor, while others have ended up playing key roles in the larger narrative. In many cases, the results have even caught Dinniman himself off guard.

In a recent development, importantly, this doesn't mean readers are deciding what Carl does or what Donut claims. Dinniman maintains creative control over his characters and their decisions, instead allowing fans to influence the external circumstances they encounter. He then has to figure out how to incorporate those choices into the story, even when readers select something completely unexpected.

It's a fairly unconventional approach to writing a fantasy series, and one that breaks the "unwritten rule" that many fantasy authors follow of keeping the world-building elements of the story very intentional and deliberate. In many ways, Dinniman allows readers to throw him curveballs as some sort of a challenge to himself to make these things work on the page, and so far there are countless examples of how it's paid off.

Some of the most notable examples include:.

Beyond Patreon, Dinniman has also incorporated suggestions from fellow writers. Author Steve Rowland, the troll stripper in the Desperado Club, was named after real-life fantasy author S.L. Rowland, who jokingly suggested his own name when Dinniman requested stripper names on Twitter.

It's pretty incredible how many beloved elements of Dungeon Crawler Carl would have been completely different without fans contributing to the creative process, and it's a major piece of what makes the series so special.

Apple is considering abandoning looks to launch an OLED iMac, according to a new supply chain report. The news comes just weeks after the first OLED Mac was released in the form of the new touchscreen MacBook Pro.

The manufacturer is remarked to be holding discussions with display partner Samsung about either delaying the planned launch or abandoning it altogether, with two reasons cited ….

Bring back a pro level iMac. The 27” 5k display was a very good size, make it a more accurate OLED display combined with the latest Apple Silicon, so former iMac owners have a choice where there is none now.

The all In one form factor remains convenient for labs, classrooms, creative departments, audio studios (home & pro), etc.

Keep the non OLED 24” display format positioned as a consumer model, plus lower its cost and you will see a sales uptick.

Industry observers note that apple’s journey into OLED screens began with the Apple Watch while other products were still using IPS LCD. The company subsequently switched to OLED for some iPhones and iPads before a long-awaited launch of the first OLED MacBook Pro back in October.

It has been revealed that it was expected that the tech giant would gradually transition to OLED across the full range of Macs over time. However, this process was expected to take a number of years, with the iMac not likely to join the party until 2029 or 2030.

The Elec today reports that the move may be delayed even further or even abandoned altogether, for two reasons: cost and demand.

The tech giant is stated to be discussing a potential delay or cancellation of the project with Samsung Display. High OLED panel costs and weak sales of existing OLED-equipped products are believed to be factors behind the reconsideration […].

Recent findings suggest that the biggest factor behind the review is cost. The iMac sells in smaller volumes than smartphones or laptops, making it difficult to maintain competitive pricing if expensive OLED panels are adopted. Weak sales of the OLED iPad Pro are also believed to have influenced the decision.

The report suggests that incoming CEO John Ternus has been reviewing the commercial viability of upgrading more products to OLED. As further evidence, the report notes Apple has sent quotation requests to LCD suppliers for an iMac screen to be rolled out in around 2029.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

2026 hasn't exactly been a banner year for Ridley Scott, who finally returned to the sci-fi genre after almost 10 years away to direct his latest movie, The Dog Stars. Based on the critically acclaimed science fiction novel of the same name by Peter Heller, Scott even tapped Josh Brolin and Jacob Elordi to lead The Dog Stars, but that didn't translate to success at the box office.

According to recent reports, the movie has since found success on VOD platforms like Prime Video and Apple TV after leaving theaters with one of the lowest-grossing box office totals of Scott's career. It won't take Scott long to seek redemption at the box office, either; he's returning to the screen in less than one year for a Treasure Island remake starring Hugh Jackman and Owen Cooper from the 2025 Netflix sensation, Adolescence.

Ridley Scott is on something of a cold streak right now after his last few movies, The Dog Stars, Gladiator II, and Napoleon all failed to dazzle at the box office, but there was a time when seeing his name on a poster meant a movie was a guaranteed hit.

It has been revealed that back in 2015, Scott teamed up with Matt Damon for The Martian, which is an adaptation of the best-selling sci-fi book of the same name from author Andy Weir, who also wrote the book that inspired Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary. The Martian is currently without a streaming home in America right now, but the demand to watch the movie at home is higher than ever. So many fans are renting or purchasing The Martian on Apple TV that it has now been in the top 10 for over 100 days now.

Industry observers note that the Martian and Project Hail Mary are quite similar, which makes sense considering both books were written by the same author, but there are some important differences. Both tales center around an astronaut who is lost millions of miles from home, but while The Martian follows Mark Watney's journey to make it back to Earth with his life, Project Hail Mary follows Ryland Grace as he attempts to save humanity from a dangerous race of space algae known as Astrophage. Project Hail Mary also features an alien named Rocky, and the film is considered a much harder sci-fi than its 2015 predecessor.

Check out The Martian on VOD platforms like Prime Video and Apple TV, and stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Matt Damon and Ridley Scott's future projects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Industry observers note that not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

Recent findings suggest that when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be noted for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

It has been revealed that because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before latest models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The glitch isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

The key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

It has been revealed that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

It has been revealed that yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

It has been revealed that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews fresh releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Recent findings suggest that brandon Sanderson has given some thought to what he’d do if he woke up as a teenager with all his adult memories intact: he’d happily pass on the opportunity. “I’ve read too many stories about time travel and it never goes well,” the Mistborn author told Woman’s World. He did, however, get out of bed the next morning and write two chapters of a book about a woman who wakes up on her 21st birthday with an entire lifetime to reconsider.

In a recent development, her name is December, and one of the things she remembers is a plague that the people she loves have yet to live through. She sets out on the River Violet to warn the king’s court, with a priestess and an aspiring fashion designer for manufacturer. Getting a royal official to take the word of a 21-year-old seriously is an immediate concern, but the harder one is deciding what to change. December can remember the people she lost, but she also knows whom she fell in love with and the children she had. Saving someone now could cost her the chance to meet somebody else later.

Sources indicate that tor Books will publish the U.S. hardcover of Brandon Sanderson’s The Fires of December on Tuesday, December 8. The 384-page edition brings the standalone Cosmere novel to bookstore shelves after an earlier release through Sanderson’s Hoid’s Storybook Collection crowdfunding campaign. Readers who prefer a physical copy can preorder the Tor edition now, while the ebook and audiobook have been available to the public since October 6, with longtime Mistborn narrator Michael Kramer reading the audio edition.

According to recent reports, four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Industry observers note that you can start with December. Sanderson groups the book with Tress of the Emerald Sea and Yumi and the Nightmare Painter under the name Hoid’s Travails. The three share a narrator in Hoid, the storyteller who turns up across the Cosmere, but each follows a different lead and tells a complete story. Readers can pick them up in any order, including anyone still working through The Stormlight Archive who’d like to spend a weekend elsewhere in Sanderson’s universe.

Sanderson had already tried two other ideas for a secret project before December came to him. Once he had those opening chapters, he wrote the first draft in about a month and printed a copy for his wife, the first person he wanted to share it with. Those same chapters are now available on his website, along with the reading he gave at Dragonsteel Nexus. It’s a good place to hear Hoid tell this one from the beginning, back when December’s biggest question about the River Violet was whether there really was a demon upstream supplying all that blood.

The Fires of December releases December 8.

If you’re still reeling from its tense atmosphere and wonder what other horror movies on Netflix capture that same sense of creeping dread and paranoia, I've got you covered.

I watch a lot of horror movies, and my top three picks for what to watch after "Obsession" are sure to fit the vibe you're looking for. Two of them come from acclaimed horror series director Mike Flanagan, while the third is a slept-on horror mystery thriller with a perfect 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes that flips the haunted house trope on its head.

So without further ado, let's dive into the best horror movies on Netflix to watch after "Obsession.".

In a recent development, just like "Obsession," "Hush" is another example of a simple premise executed well. It's also helmed by Mike Flanagan before he established himself as the king of TV horror with "The Haunting of Hill House," "Midnight Mass" and "Carrie." This slasher movie stars Flanagan's wife and long-time collaborator Kate Siegel as Maddie, a deaf and mute woman who becomes the target of a masked killer.

According to recent reports, it's lean, tightly wound horror movie that wrings a surprising amount of tension from its simple premise. The isolated setting of a house in the remote woods also adds to the atmosphere of constant unease, like you're being watched. And while Maddie is relentlessly stalked and tormented by the killer, she's never reduced to a helpless victim, which makes this one of the more empowering genre entries.

With remarkable direction from Remi Weekes (who also wrote the screenplay), strong performances from the whole cast ("Doctor Who’s" Matt Smith has a small role) and plenty of terrifying moments, "His House" is a certified chiller — and one of the best Netflix horror movies. Whenever I recommend essential horror movies to get non-horror fans into the genre, "His House" tops the list.

Recent findings suggest that "His House" follows a young refugee couple, Bol (Sope Dirisu) and Rial (Wunmi Mosaku), who are granted asylum in a small English town after fleeing war-torn South Sudan. They struggle to adjust, and straining their relationship further is the supernatural terror haunting their home that seems connected to their past. But while Rial insists something is not right and wants to move, Bol worries that making waves could get them deported. And so the two are left on their own to face whatever's haunting them.

Watch "His House" on Netflix now.

Another one from Flanagan (can you tell I'm a fan?), this trippy horror movie adds a fresh perspective to a familiar framework, where a cursed mirror not only warps the minds of the main characters, but leaves the audience questioning what's real and what's a hallucination. UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….
  • Sources indicate that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….

Sources indicate that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

The feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

According to recent reports, in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

It has been revealed that this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve stated many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It has been revealed that it would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the company found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple unveiled it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

In a recent development, “Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to upcoming users and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

Industry observers note that at this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

In a recent development, the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal mentioned. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it released – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

It has been revealed that this ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

According to recent reports, finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that 2026 has been a pretty decent year for upcoming movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar.
  • It has been revealed that thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience.
  • In fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that 2026 has been a pretty decent year for upcoming movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar. One such film is “They Will Kill You,” a gloriously bonkers mash-up of survival, comedy and horror that pits a tough-as-nails woman against a group of seriously unhinged cult members. The whole thing feels like a fever dream, with outrageous violence, ridiculous twists and enough carnage to keep you wondering what on earth you’re watching.

It has been revealed that thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience. Its theatrical run certainly didn’t do it any favors, with the movie reportedly earning approximately $19 million worldwide against a production budget of $20 million, making it a box office disappointment. That’s a shame, because while it’s not a perfect film by any means, it’s certainly not a bad one.

In fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far. It knows exactly how ridiculous it wants to be and has plenty of fun with its increasingly chaotic set pieces. I left the theater genuinely shocked by some of the things I witnessed, but also grinning at just how much fun I'd had. If you missed it on the big screen, its arrival on Prime Video is a pretty good excuse to put that right, and here’s why.

Sources indicate that “They Will Kill You” follows Asia Reaves (Zazie Beetz), a young woman who takes a live-in housekeeping job at The Virgil, a luxurious New York City apartment building, hoping to find her missing younger sister, Maria (Myha'la). However, Asia soon discovers that the building’s wealthy residents are hiding a terrifying secret: they’re members of a satanic cult that has been sacrificing unsuspecting workers for decades.

According to recent reports, when the residents attempt to make Asia their latest victim, they quickly discover she’s not quite as helpless as they expected. Trapped inside the building with seemingly no way out, Asia must fight her way through its corridors and take on an increasingly dangerous group of attackers. With time running out and Maria caught up in the cult’s aims, Asia faces a brutal fight to get them both out alive.

I’ll admit, I was a little worried “They Will Kill You” might struggle to stand out, especially arriving shortly after “Ready or Not 2,” which has a pretty similar premise involving two sisters trying to escape a cult. Thankfully, Zazie Beetz gives this film a flavor of its own. She’s an absolute badass, throwing herself into some wonderfully chaotic fight scenes and getting covered in blood more times than I can count. There’s also a noticeably angrier edge to this movie, which I really appreciated. It’s a welcome addition to the horror-comedy genre that isn’t afraid to get properly nasty.

Storytelling isn’t exactly the film’s strong suit, and I wouldn’t say it does anything particularly compelling with its characters or central plot. But that’s not really why I’d recommend it. The real draw is the action, inventive kill scenes and completely unhinged body horror. There are also some wonderfully ridiculous twists involving the cult that had me laughing, while the final act goes so completely off the rails that I was practically squealing (little hint there). It’s an absolute hoot, and I had a ridiculous amount of fun watching it.

According to recent reports, I also really enjoyed the film’s visual style. Director Kirill Sokolov uses graphic compositions that sometimes resemble comic-book panels, alongside unusual framing and some wonderfully eccentric camera angles. There are moments when the whole thing almost feels like you’re watching a video game, particularly during its more elaborate fight sequences. Yes, it’s a little unconventional, but I thought it worked brilliantly with the film’s exaggerated violence and chaotic energy. It gives “They Will Kill You” a distinct visual identity that helps it stand apart from other horror-comedies.

There’s definitely a lack of genuine character connection here, largely because the story doesn’t give you much to work with, but Beetz is such a compelling screen presence that you naturally find yourself rooting for her anyway. She’s more than capable of carrying the film, and I’d happily watch her take on another ridiculous survival scenario. I also think “They Will Kill You” has some serious cult classic potential. It might not have found its audience at the box office back in March, but I wouldn't be surprised if it earns a lot more love in the years ahead as more people discover it. Sometimes all a film needs is a second chance, and this one certainly deserves it.

Stream "They Will Kill You" on Prime Video now.

Alix is a Senior Streaming Writer at Tom’s Guide, which basically means watching the best movies and TV reveals and then writing about them. It’s a dream job for someone who’s been obsessed with storytelling since she first figured out how to work a remote.

Before joining Tom’s Guide, Alix honed her skills as a staff writer with outlets like Screen Rant and Bough Digital, where she discovered her love for the entertainment industry.

She heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.
