What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most crucial tech manufacturer in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy.
  • At least, that’s the simple version of the story.
  • Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, says Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most crucial tech manufacturer in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy. The most valuable tech in the world — Huang’s super-powered computer chips — are smuggled into China or installed into data centers connected to America’s greatest rival. Above it all, the possibility of a super-intelligent AI, a true artificial mind, looms — and its creator will be positioned to rule the world.

At least, that’s the simple version of the story. But the real picture of the great geopolitical AI race is both more complex and more unbelievable than the tale of spies and smuggling that’s playing out in the press right now. China wants the U.S.’s chips — that much is clear. But why? And what can our only real rival power actually do with them? To answer this, Rolling Stone spoke with two experts in the Chinese tech sector, who pulled back the curtain on what the superpower actually wants when it comes to AI — and why it’s willing to use sex, smuggling and lies to get there.

Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, says Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.

According to recent reports, the first is as a straight race to one goal: creating a truly intelligent AI that surpasses human intelligence in all general tasks and can improve itself autonomously. In the industry, this is known as AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence. This point of view holds that the first country or organization to achieve true AGI will have an earth-shattering advantage over any competition in economics, war, medicine, and technology. Basically, it sets the world of AI up as a winner-take-all race. Many U.S. officials — including, at times, Trump himself — have made this argument, alongside many of the private sector CEOs actually working on the technology.

“If you start with that assumption, then the effort to slow down China is nearly existential,” Chan claims. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The biggest advantage the U.S. has is Nvidia’s chips. The most powerful computer chips in the world are made by one facility in Taiwan, using incredibly complex and rare machines manufactured by one tech giant in the Netherlands. It is a process so detailed and scientifically complex that it might as well be magic. Other companies can make chips, of course, but none of them can make chips as well as the single manufacturing company in Taiwan that Nvidia and most of the U.S. tech giants use. AI companies need these chips, and these chips alone, to run the most advanced AI models — which is why the U.S. has done a lot to limit China’s access to them, setting export controls on who Nvidia can sell their chips to and which countries they can be shipped into.

Sources indicate that because of this constraint, the Chinese don’t really see AI the same way as most of the U.S. industry does.

Instead of an existential threat, Chan says, the second way to look at AI is a very powerful technology that will not necessarily lead to some massive strategic advantage for the first team past the AGI post. That makes the AI race a longer-term game, decided more by which power can holistically incorporate the advances of super-computing into its society and economy, which China has largely focused on doing.

Recent findings suggest that “What we’re kind of seeing unfold in the future is two different markets,” said Kenton Thibaut, a China expert at the Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab. The U.S. is focused on “frontier” systems — the absolute cutting-edge AI, powered by their chip advantage — while China is supplying “near frontier” technology that hits different parts of the market for AI technology. In China, Thibaut said, AI is viewed as a “general purpose” technology that should be harnessed for practical use as swiftly as possible, rather than a more conceptual race to the furthest frontier. Related Content Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire Trump Says He ‘Can’t Speak To’ Whether Russia is a Friend to America Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi Your Favorite THC Drinks Are About to Be Illegal.

Recent findings suggest that “All of the [Chinese] policies and major policy pronouncements and planning around AI have to do with ‘How do we make this useful in society?’” Thibaut said. “I haven’t seen anything like that in the US.”.

Industry observers note that “[China’s] version of winning is being able to benefit the most from AI,” Chan states. “Integrate it in their economy, automate their factories, speed up drug discovery, et cetera. [They want it to] help them win across all these other domains, rather than this singular focus on achieving AGI.”.

According to recent reports, it’s a philosophical difference that is fueled by the physical constraints that the Chinese tech sector faces. The U.S. has access to more computing power than any other nation, allowing them to push the envelope. Companies like Anthropic have asked the U.S. government to regulate them more, fearful that their AI models will run out of control. In China, these discussions are scarce, Thibaut claims, because the hardware they’re working with basically makes them moot — and the Chinese government is predisposed to prevent any societal disruptions. Instead, Chinese AI firms are usually focused on doing more with less — creating working, practical products and applications of AI that get the most out of whatever computing power they can harness.

And in some cases, that’s where the spies come in. The Nvidia honeypot scandal was largely controversial because it included a woman who ran a Singaporean front company that set up data centers in Southeast Asia stocked with Taiwan-made super-chips, and then leased the use of those chips to Chinese companies. Chan refers to this loophole, and the broader Chinese project of getting their hands on American tech, as a “bridge” to the country’s real goal: separating themselves from the Western “tech stack,” while still retaining competitive computing power. Eventually, Chan notes, China wants to have its own version of the super-manufacturers in Taiwan, its own version of the very best chips — but until then, it has to use more subtle methods to get what it wants.

Industry observers note that “If they want to keep pace today, they do still need access to Nvidia chips now,” Chan notes. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special The Making of My Chemical Romance's 'The Black Parade'.

In a recent development, some parts of the U.S. government may be helping them achieve that. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik had been very lax with Nvidia and Huang personally, allowing the firm to continue selling to companies that the U.S. knew were linked with China. While Trump has mentioned he views AI as a winner-take-all race, Reuters reported that his administration also signed off on the sale of 900,000 AI chips to Chinese companies in one six-month period, and his own AI Czar David Sacks has explicitly advocated for selling more chips directly to China.

China, then, has allies to go along with its spies — and it seems that one way or another, it’s getting all the chips it needs.

Gemini Notebook's Latest Interactive Site Builder Is Much More Useful Than I Expected

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • It has been revealed that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • Recent findings suggest that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something fresh. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

It has been revealed that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

Recent findings suggest that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

According to recent reports, to make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

With a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but states you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Sources indicate that here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

According to recent reports, the finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a newly introduced window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

Recent findings suggest that I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

It has been revealed that everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

For something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

In a recent development, maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a substantial family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a upcoming website.

Bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While many Yellowjackets fans are struggling to cope with the inevitable end, for its series creators, it was the right time to land the plane.

Discussing the fourth and final season with Deadline, Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson explained that they didn’t want to “run the risk of overstaying our welcome” with another season when they were reaching the conclusion “more rapidly.”.

“We’d always said that we had pitched a five-season strategy, but we’d always given the caveat that we felt like the show would tell us when it wanted to end, and just in the breaking of this story, it started to feel like we were sort of moving towards the end more rapidly,” explained Nickerson. “And so, then the decision kind of became, ‘OK, do we sort of squeeze a lot into Season 4 or run the risk of overstaying our welcome out of the fifth season?’ We chose to try to squeeze it in, and that ended up really just kind of working out nicely from our perspective.

According to recent reports, “The show has always had to be very kind of efficient, with the storytelling. It’s a double ensemble with a lot of story that we’re telling, and so I think we’ve gotten pretty good or comfortable kind of operating a at a certain pace and a certain kind of grammar, for lack of a better word, and so that was what we did,” he added. Watch on Deadline.

As Nickerson explained it was an “incredible gift” to know they were ending after Season 4, Lyle noted that they were “reinvigorated” to get to return to civilization, which had always been their strategy for the final season.

Sources indicate that “We had been looking forward to that for so long now. It was part of the original pitch, and to finally get there—everything, when you’re pitching a show, it all feels like a pipe dream,” remarked Lyle. “You don’t think you’re actually going to be able to do any of this, especially something that you know is only gonna be if you get a first season, a second season, a third season. So, to actually reach that point and get to dive in, it reinvigorated everybody.”.

In Yellowjackets, a 1996 New Jersey soccer team’s plane crashes in the Canadian wilderness, where they struggle to survive while they’re stranded for 19 months as a dark supernatural force seemingly lurks in the woods. Meanwhile, their adult counterparts cope with the memories of what went down in the wilderness.

With newly introduced episodes available to stream Fridays on Paramount+ with Premium Proposal, the fourth and final season sees the Yellowjackets rescued and returned home, where they must adjust to civilization and take their secrets to the grave.

Catherine, the Princess of Wales will discuss her cancer battle in an upcoming documentary special that will raise money for the hospital that treated her.

Heal: A Princess of Wales Story will air November 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC. The documentary follows Kate Middleton as she reflects on her cancer battle while completing the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the span of 24 hours — this past June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the hospital where she was treated; proceeds from the distribution of Heal will also benefit Royal Marsden.

“Cancer does change you. It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” the Princess of Wales says in the trailer.

In a recent development, “It’s clear we’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone. Things can renew and grow. After it is through pain that we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that.”.

The news of Middleton’s initial diagnosis was disclosed to the public in March 2024, following an abdominal surgery in January. In a video statement, Middleton remarked, “At the time, it was thought that my condition was non-cancerous,” referring to her surgery. “The surgery was successful, however, tests after the operation on cancer had been present,” she added. According to recent reports, by September 2024, the Princess of Wales revealed that she had completed the treatment. “The cancer journey is complex, scary, and unpredictable for everyone, especially those closest to you,” Middleton wrote at the time. “With humility, it also brings you face to face with your own vulnerabilities in a way you have never considered before, and with that, a new perspective on everything.”.

In January 2025, Middleton declared, “It is a relief to now be in remission and I remain focused on recovery.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other demonstrates dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

This time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It promptly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

It has been revealed that A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

Industry observers note that mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that swiftly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

Industry observers note that peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

The latest Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

Four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

According to recent reports, ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. It also summarizes utility records from a major regional ice storm. Finally, it outlines how to choose corridors, strategy restoration and keep crews and the public safe around covered conductors.

The Making of My Chemical Romance’s ‘The Black Parade’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade.
  • Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by latest music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.
  • Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a newly introduced vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade. It was Tommy in a white belt and eyeliner, vastly expanding the band’s sonic palette beyond the punk-thrash of their first two albums. It felt like the beginning of what should have been a long, ambitious fresh phase of My Chem’s career, but instead, they released the underrated Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys in 2010 and broke up three years later.

Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by latest music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

Welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a newly introduced vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut. That album’s producer, Rob Cavallo (who also worked on much of Green Day‘s discography, among many other projects) joined Rolling Stone by Zoom for an in-depth look at the making of a 21st-century rock masterpiece.

What did My Chem first play for you that got you excited to be involved in this album?They were interviewing other guys as well, but I’ll never forget, ’cause it was so freezing cold in Latest York, and we went to SIR, and they played me a few things. But the one that blew my mind was “Mama.” When I heard that, I remember just jumping off the couch just going, “Oh, my God, you guys. That is so great and original,” and you could tell it was part of a deeper picture of something, even though I was new to the band. It felt key to me right away that this band was existing on a higher conceptual level.

Recent findings suggest that that song sounds like the Doors version of “Alabama Song.” It’s very un-punk at first, and then it kicks into the—The heavy part, right. Yeah, I kinda likened it in a weird way rhythmically to the Doors. I was also thinking of [the Rolling Stones’] “Mother’s Little Helper.” Almost like you could see the Cossacks-style Russian dancing to it. It’s like this sort of head-bopping thing that just felt very edgy, and very anti-establishment rock in a weird way. It was definitely like the we-don’t-give-a-fuck kind of rock. According to recent reports, but then there was this story in there. I was like, “What is this guy going on about? What is happening here? This is heavy stuff.” So that’s why I jumped up off the couch on that song.

In a recent development, and of course, a lot of the record at that point had not been written. And then I got this call and they said, “Meet us at this steakhouse near SIR.” And I remember walking there and I thought my legs were gonna freeze off. And then we got in and we had the greatest dinner ever, and they said, “All right, you wanna be our producer?” I said, “Yeah, I do.” And that was it. They decided a couple hours after the first meeting.

In a recent development, do you think your enthusiasm put it over the top for them? Obviously it couldn’t have hurt that you had just done American Idiot, which had similar levels of ambition.I think I was told that they liked what I remarked about the music, and they probably liked that I had done two records that I think stood out in their minds. Yeah, I had just done American Idiot, which was of course really substantial and was working, and I think they liked that. And then I think the other record they mentioned was Jawbreaker, Dear You, which is a band and an album that had an infamous history of being a dismal failure, in a way, commercially when it first came out.

According to recent reports, but also then received its just deserts many years later, in the fact that it was now considered one of the seminal emo records of all time. And of course, we all know the history about how the band got back together and then all of a sudden on one show there were 60,000 people singing every word to every song on that record. But at the same time we also know that Kurt Cobain was, like, one of their biggest supporters — they were opening for Nirvana. So it was kinda cool. Industry observers note that how did My Chem define their ambitions on that first day?It wasn’t necessarily something that we actually talked about. I think Gerard [Way] had it in his mind, but a lot of it happened when we went into this place called the Paramour. The band was looking for a place where they could live and work and write.

According to recent reports, A sort of haunted mansion, apparently.Oh, it was haunted all right. Crazy stuff was happening all the time. You could just feel the vibes of the insanity that was happening — doors closing by themselves, and probably the eeriest hallway. To this day, I still remember that hallway going down to where the bedrooms were on the top floor, and it just looked like you were in the scariest movie. And the coat of arms and the polar bear, the stuffed polar bear, all the weird stuff that was just everywhere.

And it was also kinda freezing in there. It was such an old building that we had to bring in space heaters, and so a lot of the writing actually ended up taking place over a couple of months in that particular space. And Mikey [Way] eventually, as you probably heard, he had to move out. He couldn’t take it after a while. It was just too scary.

According to recent reports, but we had a lot of fun there, and we got a lot of the work done. So the record, I would say, was probably 90 percent written by the time, or 95 percent written by the time we got out of there and headed to the studio. With, of course, the notable exception of the song “Black Parade” itself, that has its own sort of strange and storied history.

According to recent reports, while they’re writing in the house, where are you and what are you doing?Every day, Monday through Friday, I’d show up with my engineer, Doug McKean, and I set up some fancy microphones in this giant, crazy living room that they had. The great room in that house looked like it was, like, 1,500 square feet. And we put the band in there with a PA, like a smaller PA, so that we could record whatever the band was writing and doing. So the writing was done almost live.

It has been revealed that gerard liked to just sing over the band. And someone would bring in a riff and we would just start jamming and recording. And the great news is that all of those recordings actually are now available online. I think there was a significant box set of these live two-track recordings that are sort of the precursor — they’re the demos that we made the album from.

Yeah, those are available to stream now.We put them on these DAT tapes. I had a special digital audio tape recorder, which was basically a tape that would be equivalent to CD quality. We would set about writing and creating and capturing these compositions, and working on the structure of them and what have you, so that we could then go into the studio, which is, of course, radically more expensive, and make the record.

Was Gerard having his night terrors at the house, and did he think they were caused by the house?You’d have to ask him if they were being caused by the house. But one thing for sure is the house had an effect on him, because it was a strangely haunted, dark place.

In a recent development, and he did talk about the night terrors, and he did talk about that he was going through a lot of things at that particular time. I think he was, like, a young man at the cusp at that time. I didn’t know where he was with his significant-other situation. There might have been something going on there. I don’t really know. But I would say this, I could tell he had a great record in him.

They’re a very emotional band, and they’re the nicest people. They’re very cordial to each other, and everything is on the up and up. But they also kinda would wear their hearts on their sleeves; if they were upset about something else in life, you could hear about it, you know? I was there to be very supportive. But the one thing for sure is that nothing ever got in the way of the music. We went to work. It was serious. We seriously worked 10, 12 hours a day.

Industry observers note that when Mikey has to leave because it’s psychologically oppressive, does it make anyone else wonder, “Hey, maybe we should get the hell out of here too?”I think there was some conversation about it, but I also think, certainly, there were financial considerations. I think that there was a lease that we had to let expire, and, like, where were they gonna stay if they go, and what other money is that? ‘Cause we were responsible and [we were] on a budget.

And you’re writing all this great stuff, so why not stay?That’s the other thing. The vibe in the daytime and into the evening, in terms of getting work done, it was working. You’re really correct on that.

Industry observers note that so you go in the studio. Let’s talk about “Welcome to the Black Parade,” which started as “The Five of Us Are Dying.”So what was interesting is that it was a song that we thought was good, and we knew we were gonna put it on the record.

According to recent reports, but there [were] two things about it that kinda didn’t work. One was, I remember there was, “What’s the intro gonna be?” And “Do we just pop into the song?” And it never felt totally settled. And then the other thing was the chords on the chorus were… If you listen to “Five of Us Are Dying,” you’ll see that the chord structure was slightly different, and it didn’t feel like a hit record. It just felt like an OK song.

So what happened?I really gotta give credit to Gerard and the band. So I, for whatever reason, one day revealed up to the studio early. And nobody was around, and we were at the Eldorado Studio in Burbank. And so I would sometimes sit there and just play the piano in the morning and just get my ears opened up and refreshed or whatever.

And lo and behold, Gerard shows up five minutes later. We were a good half an hour, 40 minutes before everybody. And so I’m just playing the piano, and he liked that ’cause I could play Queen songs and whatever. I remember him pointing at me once when we were up at the Paramour mansion, and I started playing things. He goes, “Oh, hey, listen to Cavallo. He can actually do shit on the piano. We should use that.”.

So now here we are, like a month or two later, and we’re at Eldorado. And he goes to me, “Can you play…” And he cited the graduation theme, like “Pomp and Circumstance.” He goes, “But can you do that, but just make it go down?” And so I had one of those weird moments where I said to myself, “Don’t think, just play.” And my fingers literally started playing, and Gerard almost immediately started singing, “When I was a young boy…” And it was really a magical thing, and we had a little voice note recorder or voice memo thingy, and we recorded it, and he goes, “OK, so this is the parade.” We were thinking of it as being, like, an interstitial moment in the record where you would hear a parade from half a mile away or a quarter mile away, and it’d start very light.

According to recent reports, that’s why I played it with one finger at first. And then I started playing it with two hands, and then I started playing it as major as I could make it — loud. And then, now that the parade has passed you, it gets quieter again, right? So I worked it all the way back up to just the single-note thing, right? And the thing probably lasted two, two and a half minutes. And so then the idea was, OK, we’re gonna have marching bands, and we’re gonna have orchestral percussion and the horns and the whole thing.

But I went away with my family for a few days, and when I got back on Monday, Gerard notes, “You gotta hear this. You gotta hear this.” And what they had done was they had taken the first half of “The Black Parade” and attached it to what would become the extended intro to [“The Five of Us Are Dying”]. And I was like, “Oh, my God, that totally works.”.

What else did they change?I think Ray [Toro] or somebody fixed the chords on the chorus. The chorus became much more sing-along. And then all of a sudden that made sense. But what it really also did was, because we had a marching band and giant orchestrations in the intro, it afforded us the ability for me as a producer to say, “Now I can afford to have all these big orchestrations and all those things during the body of the song,” which normally you wouldn’t have a reason to do. It raised the bar of the song creatively to such a level that we could do something that in a weird way maybe on a pop-punk record had not been done before.

It has been revealed that I remember I played it for one of my great mentors, Lenny Waronker, who was the longtime president of Warner’s, famous dude, and he went, “Holy shit. What the hell is that? I’ve never heard anything like that.” It actually worked, you know? So I remember thinking, “Wow, Lenny likes it. Yay.”.

In a recent development, let’s talk about “Teenagers.”He really did mean what he was saying, but sometimes an artist can do what they would call a throwaway. Because he was concerned with — this is when Columbine happened, and kids were getting violent. And that song almost didn’t make the record.

Sources indicate that what happened was there were some people that thought, “This is like an old-school rock & roll song.” And the argument was, “Why are we doing an old rock & roll song?” Like what they call a I-IV-V [chord-progression] song, like Chuck Berry. But what’s great about that is that my argument was, how do you write a contemporary I-IV-V song that is so great? And have the lyric be that meaningful? To me, that was the argument to do it. Right?

It’s just an crucial record. And to be fair, it worked out, you know? Everybody agreed. It took a week or two. It was definitely a conversation, ’cause if you do listen to the record, I admit that it is an outlier on the album.

According to recent reports, but there was just something so compelling about that. At the beginning, it wasn’t obvious even how to cut it, but we did. I remember we all took turns at, “What should the bass be like?” You know? And I think Ray actually kinda figured it out. But anyway, the point is that the record came out and look what happened. It just exploded.

I believe it was your phone call that got Liza Minnelli on “Mama.”Yeah, so we were talking about, on “Mama,” who should play Mother War? The idea of this was like Mother War is this weird character. And there was a wonderful lady — Liz Rosenberg, Madonna’s publicist. And so I was kicking around Warner’s, like, does anybody know Liza Minnelli? I think it was Gerard’s idea. It was definitely the band’s idea. And I stated, “Let me see if I can get it.” So I called Liz Rosenberg and she said, “I can do it. I think I can get her.” And anyways, the fucking miracles, she did it. She got her.

What was working with Liza like?One of the things that was so great about Liza is that she was so consummately professional that we got the takes that we wanted, and she was not done. She was like, “No, I need to keep doing this. Let me keep trying. Let me perfect this. Let me get this crying part down. Let me figure out how I can truly nail this performance.” And her attention to detail, I have to say, I was just so blown away by her.

It has been revealed that we haven’t necessarily had a ton of great guitar solo albums this century, but this is definitely one of them. Do any memories stand out?Both Ray and Frank [Iero] are great guitar players, and they did amazing things. But the thing that always stands out is the song “Dead!” And that first solo, because what’s crazy about that solo is that that happened by accident. It was supposed to just be the chords, and we weren’t gonna actually have a solo there. The chords were, like, enough.

But Ray being as great guitar player as he is, I think we just hit record or whatever, and he had the guitar in his hand, and he just ripped that solo, actually just as like a warmup or something. And we went, “We gotta use it. We gotta use it,” and he was like, “No, no. We can’t use it. We can’t use that. That’s just…” And then we printed a rough mix of the whole thing and we kept living with it, and over the course of the next week or two, I was like, “Ray, we gotta use it. It’s too good.” And eventually he said, “OK, fuck, we’ll use the solo.” But what’s amazing is it shows you how good a player he is, because that was something that was — how do I explain it? — an off-the-cuff, unplanned solo. How good is that? That this guy could just do that without even thinking about it.

In a recent development, the band hung out in a house for two months writing, and then recorded at a great studio. Would it be very difficult to get all that together in the current music industry, on a major label?Yes and no. It’s funny, if you look at the budgets back then for a band like that and the way the music business is now, it’s really comparing apples and oranges, right? I don’t think that Paramour was, like, that expensive, because if it’s 15 or 20 grand a month and you do it for two months, and you’re housing like five, six, seven guys, that’s actually cheap. And also rehearsing. That’s actually kinda inexpensive if you’re thinking about it in terms of real estate. If you were to pay a rehearsal place and hotels and all that kind of stuff, it’d be a lot more.

Recent findings suggest that and then we went to Eldorado, which was not an A++ expensive three-grand-a-day place. It was actually more in the middle level. Like $1,200 or so — and I think we were able to crank that album out in, tops, two and a half months. So 10 weeks or something. That was a budget-conscious record, which made sense because they were a band on their way up. The prior record did well, but it wasn’t like there was like oodles of money running around all over the place.

I was kinda known as a producer that could stay on budget. So we probably did this one in the $200,000 to $250,000 range, but that’s just a total fucking guess.

Was there any sense, working on Black Parade, that this was a band about to make just one more album and then not make one for a very long time?There was no indication during making Black Parade that it was gonna be only one more album, but there was indication near the end of Danger Days that there were feelings afoot, shall we say.

The band has noted there’s a newly introduced album coming. Are you working with them now?No, I was supposed to go see them at the Hollywood Bowl, and then I got the flu, so I didn’t go. But I’ve been in contact with Ray and Mikey. I really don’t know what their plans are. Meanwhile, you have a hit record again, 20 years later. It just shows you the state of the music business being in such a weird place. But it’s also a good place. When I looked at it, just the idea that there’s a new piece of vinyl — I think when a band is really good and makes really good music and there’s also a bit of a scarcity about it, right? They haven’t made music in a long time. You put out this new piece of product and the hardcore fans will buy. I actually bought one myself the other day. I was at Amoeba and I mentioned, “You know what? I should just buy one for good luck.”.

You pushed it over the top. It would’ve been Number Two if you didn’t jump in there.I bought a whole one copy at $40. It’s amazing, and they sold something like, I think, 70,000 of them or something. And I think that was just in the United States, unless that was worldwide, I don’t know. But I also know it was Number One in the U.K. But what’s interesting is those numbers are, in a weird way, like old-school, unheard-of numbers, because if you sell 70,000 at $40 list price, the gross is 2.8 million bucks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As many SAG-AFTRA members struggle to qualify for health insurance, the union is taking the issue to the U.S. government.

On Friday, Screen Actors Guild President Sean Astin announced the President’s Healthcare Task Force to address the “broken healthcare system” while several actors have faced losing their insurance under the union’s minimum eligibility requirements.

According to recent reports, “This is a critical moment, where both our members and the public at large can no longer wait for relief from a broken healthcare system,” he mentioned in a statement. “Our SAG-AFTRA Health Plan is healthy and strong, but a substantial majority of our members do not qualify. For our members who don’t qualify, there is very little that can be done to provide coverage.”.

According to recent reports, astin added, “SAG-AFTRA has supported efforts to expand healthcare for all through the AFL-CIO. This task force seeks a new level of participation in the national movement to expand care for everyone. We will actively engage with policymakers, gather allies and provide a structured way for our members to participate formally in the process. The President’s Healthcare Task Force will be an instrument of support in the movement for universal healthcare.” Watch on Deadline.

The SAG-AFTRA National Board voted unanimously on Friday to form the Task Force, which seeks to mobilize SAG-AFTRA’s collective strength and public influence to fight for universal access to affordable, comprehensive and reliable health care.

SAG’s upcoming initiative comes amid financial scrutiny for the union following National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s recent contract renewal, after his salary surpassed $1M in 2023.

Pion Interceptor: WebRTC for Hackers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, pion was started with unique use cases in mind.
  • Pion's Interceptor design was heavily influenced by GStreamer Pipelines.
  • Provide a library of elements for owners to build pipelines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pion was started with unique use cases in mind. Existing WebRTC software was very good at handling popular use cases. It was difficult to build unique/niche things with it though. This idea has always been at the core of Pion. Pion Interceptor was designed with the idea that we make it easy for developers to build their cool ideas. Without the frustration of forking/modifying Pion.

Pion's Interceptor design was heavily influenced by GStreamer Pipelines. With GStreamer pipelines you have a pipeline of elements that modify media. Things like resizing, croping or rotating media. A simple visualization like this.

We wanted the same for Pion. Provide a library of elements for owners to build pipelines. The default interceptors would give a good experience. Or you can bring your own to have custom behavior if you need it.

An Interceptor is started when Bind is called on it. Bind passes a StreamInfo that contains all the metadata about the stream. When a Interceptor is no longer Unbind is called. Then each RTP/RTCP packet is passed through in the Reader/Writer methods. This allows a user to process incoming/outgoing packets.

The following is the full API as generated by go doc.

Industry observers note that A NACK is how WebRTC handles packet loss. A receiver sends a NACK so that the sender knows to re-send a packet. The following is a minimal example to show how it could be implemented.

This simple NACK implementation detects gaps between packets and sends NACKs back to senders to fix a stream with packet loss.

Today we provide these pre-made interceptors:.

When building your interceptors keep these in mind.

Order Matters - Register the stats interceptor before the NACK responder so it can count retransmitted RTP packets. Registering stats after the responder means retransmissions bypass it. Incoming NACKs are counted in either order.

According to recent reports, don't forget to read - Interceptors are fired by you calling Read. If your application doesn't do a Read things like Stats or NACKs won't happen.

But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one of the year's most anticipated sports films has finally landed on Prime, delivering a biopic football fans have long awaited: a profile of gridiron great John Madden. Nicolas Cage plays the titular icon who not only brought wins to the field, but also conquered the broadcast booth and the gaming sector by helping launch the blockbuster video game franchise of the same name.

Industry observers note that written and directed by David O. Russell, "Madden" spans an impressive career that saw the outspoken coach lead the Oakland Raiders to an unlikely Super Bowl win under upcoming team owner Al Davis. The film also spotlights his legendary broadcasting run — where his infectious enthusiasm gave fans a masterclass in football’s strategic decisions — alongside his partnership with EA Sports founder Trip Hawkins to create the sports game to emulate.

Sources indicate that while "Madden" arrives after a drought of memorable sports biopics, we once enjoyed decades of exquisitely filmed profiles of real-life icons. Whether they toiled on the diamond or battled for recognition on the gridiron, these legends inspired us with their courage, tenacity, and business smarts. If you’re looking to tap into your inner jock with remarkable stories you’ll long remember, check out the top five sports biopics you can stream right now.

Recent findings suggest that if you haven’t seen Robert De Niro’s Oscar-winning turn as 1940s boxing champ Jake LaMotta in "Raging Bull," stop what you’re doing and watch this beaut of a film. Martin Scorsese’s powerhouse drama tracks LaMotta from a hungry middleweight amateur to a ferocious fighter feared across the country.

Sources indicate that while his personal life imploded from unrelenting jealousy and rage, the boxing scenes are where sports fans will find the real magic. The visceral sound design and the cinematographer’s eye for putting us right inside the ropes remain just as stunning today as when the film dropped in 1980.

Stream "Raging Bull" free on Tubi.

It has been revealed that football has its share of rewatchable classics, from "Friday Night Lights" to "Any Given Sunday," but "Rudy" stands out for anyone who knows the struggle of being told you aren't athletic enough to get a shot. The 1993 favorite introduces us to Daniel "Rudy" Ruettiger (poignantly played by Sean Astin), a plucky blue-collar kid from Joliet, Illinois, who dreams of suiting up for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish.

In a recent development, at 5-foot-6 and barely 160 pounds, he’s an underdog in every sense, and the road to glory is paved with painful stones. Even after making it onto campus, trying out for the squad brings relentless bullying and bruised pride, yet his work ethic never wavers. When he finally earns his spot on the roster, we’re left with a heartwarming reminder from the real Ruettiger: you’re never too small to make a difference.

In a recent development, A rare biopic focused on a front-office executive, "Moneyball" is astonishing on multiple levels. Based on the bestseller of the same name, this 2011 hit follows Oakland Athletics general manager Billy Beane (Brad Pitt), who teams up with a nerdy stats genius (Jonah Hill) to rebuild a roster gutted by the loss of star players. Instead of chasing pricey sluggers, they recruit strictly on underappreciated metrics like on-base percentage.

In a recent development, the story hooks you even if you aren't a die-hard MLB fan, shining a light on the statisticians and math aficionados who rescued managers stuck in 1980s-era habits of buying big names. "Moneyball" lingers long after the credits roll thanks to Aaron Sorkin’s razor-sharp screenplay, which crackles just as intensely during tense boardroom negotiations as it does out on the diamond. In our AI-driven, stats-hungry era, it holds up effortlessly.

Rent/buy "Moneyball" on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that chadwick Boseman shone in "Black Panther," but his commanding turn as Jackie Robinson in "42" deserves every ounce of applause. Focusing on the mental resilience baseball’s first Black player had to forge amid rampant racism, the 2013 drama is a poignant portrait of both a generational talent and a cultural hero.

It has been revealed that even as his own teammates hurled insults to his face, Robinson forced the wider baseball community to judge players on their merits rather than the color of their skin. The film’s message lands so powerfully because it highlights rather than tells, skipping didactic lectures and letting the tension breathe. We’re given space to reflect on Robinson’s massive impact while marveling at his rare gifts on the field, making it the kind of movie you want to revisit every few years to see how sports can open doors it once slammed shut.

Industry observers note that in 2023, we were treated to a rare twist on the genre: a sports biopic where the star athlete never appears on screen. Neither Michael Jordan nor his likeness ever shows up in "Air," directed by and starring Ben Affleck—and yet the film completely works. Set in 1984, it follows Nike CEO Phil Knight (Affleck) as he tasks talent scout Sonny Vaccaro (Matt Damon) and marketing exec Howard White (Chris Tucker) with landing a young rookie on a shoestring budget.

Industry observers note that most of us see a pair of Jordans without realizing MJ still earns a cut of every sneaker sold today, all thanks to savvy deal-making and a sharp mother. In a tight 110 minutes, "Air" reveals what makes a custom shoe design pop—and how the Nike-Jordan agreement sparked the modern era of athlete equity partnerships. Along the way, Viola Davis steals the show as Jordan’s mother, blending sharp business acumen with a fierce commitment to securing her son’s legacy.

If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

There’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

In a recent development, if you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that you obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

You can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that if you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luca Guadagnino has to return some videotapes. The Oscar-nominated director is passing on Scott Z. Burns‘ American Psycho adaptation.

While appearing on Deadline’s Crew Call podcast, Guadagnino told Anthony D’Allesandro that he is no longer attached to the projects, two years after we exclusively revealed he and Burns were adapting Bret Easton Ellis’ 1991 novel.

“Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script,” said Guadagnino. “Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it’s not happening.”.

According to recent reports, in October 2024, Deadline revealed that Guadagnino was in final talks with Lionsgate to direct Burns’ adaptation, which would be produced by Frenesy Films, and executive produced by Sam Pressman, the son of Edward R. Pressman, producer of 2000 original movie, through his organization Pressman Film. Watch on Deadline.

Serving as a brief respite from the years-long casting hunt for the next James Bond, there was plenty of speculation about who would play Patrick Bateman. One actor to campaign for the role was Patrick Schwarzenegger, while Guadagnino’s Queer (2024) star Drew Starkey noted he read the “amazing” script.

But in February, Ellis claimed that multiple high-profile actors “have turned it down,” adding that Burns had since completed a new draft after the unnamed talent passed on the previous version.

Ellis teased that the film would be “completely different” from Mary Harron’s 2000 adaptation of American Psycho, which starred Christian Bale as homicidal investment banker Patrick Bateman, the literary character that Ellis created as a satirical take on masculinity. The Harron-helmed adaptation also starred Justin Theroux, Josh Lucas, Chloë Sevigny, Reese Witherspoon, Jared Leto, Willem Dafoe and more.

  • According to recent reports, xc is a heterogeneous data-parallel language.
  • This repository holds the compiler, its GUI framework and the tools and applications built with them.
  • It is one repository, but it is worked on as several separate streams, and each stream stays inside its own tree.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, xc is a heterogeneous data-parallel language. Write an ordinary loop, in xc or in C, and xcc runs it across every CPU core, on the GPU through Metal, CUDA, Vulkan or WebGPU, across several GPUs from different vendors at once, or on a GPU on another machine, and keeps whichever is fastest. The kernels are generated by xcc itself and carried in the executable, so a build needs no GPU toolkit. Documentation, benchmarks and downloads are at https://compile-xc.org.

This repository holds the compiler, its GUI framework and the tools and applications built with them.

It is one repository, but it is worked on as several separate streams, and each stream stays inside its own tree.

Two rules keep the streams' work apart:.

Pull requests, from outside contributors and from the streams alike, keep main always gated:.

Industry observers note that private/ is not part of the repository. It is ignored by git and holds the working rules, the notes on open and fixed bugs, and other material that is never published. Nothing under it is ever committed.

Build and install the compiler first (see compiler/USAGE.md), then build whichever other tree you are working in against it.

Settings that depend on your machines, such as the Linux test host or the location of the GEM desktop sources, live in build.env at the repository root. Copy build.env.template to build.env and fill in the values you need. build.env is ignored by git. A variable left empty turns off the step that needs it.

According to recent reports, pull requests are welcome. CONTRIBUTING.md says how a change gets into main: the contributor licence agreement you sign once, where changes go, and how to build and test with an installed release. Everyone taking part agrees to the code of conduct. Security problems are reported privately, as SECURITY.md describes.

According to recent reports, every benchmark figure on the site is measured on hardware the project has bought, and the machines that matter most for data-parallel work are expensive. A loan or donation goes straight into the compiler: a back end and a runtime tuned on the device, kept working by being tested on it every release, and its figures published beside the others. We would most like:.

If you make or sell hardware like this and would like xc to run well on it, write to xc@oobergeek.net.

My apologies but I wasn't great at keeping private details out of the ~3000 or so checkins made to get this far, and the thought of going back and changing everything didn't really appeal. So, clean start, and I'll be more diligent from now on...

Sources indicate that amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Recent findings suggest that then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

Sources indicate that if your lawn is buried under a blanket of fallen leaves like mine, raking them up has likely turned a routine chore into a real slog. When wet conditions set in, clearing leaves off the grass often turns into a time-consuming hassle.

It has been revealed that and while my go-to steel rake has been my lifesaver, I often worry I might be causing damage to my healthy lawn in the process. This is especially the case when the leaves all clump together, making it a challenge to leave my grass spotless and debris-free.

It has been revealed that I called on an expert to shed light on this and offer top tips on how to rake wet leaves without pulling up blades of grass. So before you get out to tackle your leaves on your lawn, here are expert-approved tips this season.

With wet weather making lawn care challenging, is raking damp leaves actually safe for my grass? “Yes, although wet leaves are heavier, stick together, and can be much more difficult to rake, blow, or vacuum,” states Karen Musgrave, Horticulturalist at Hicks Nurseries.

“The bigger concern for your lawn is allowing a thick layer of leaves to remain there for an extended period of time. A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.”.

A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.

In a recent development, in addition, leaving wet leaves sitting on your lawn over time can smother the grass, blocking essential nutrients from reaching the roots and making it prone to mold and fungal diseases. This can lead to patchy or thinning grass that will need urgent repair come springtime.

Sources indicate that so what is the correct way to rake wet leaves without pulling up grass and harming my lawn? Experts agree that choosing the right tools is essential to do the job — and keep your yard intact.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, “If the lawn is wet, avoid being overly aggressive with a rake because you can pull at the grass,” advises Musgrave. “ For the lawn, I would choose a lightweight leaf rake with a wide head rather than a heavier garden rake.

“It gives you more control around garden beds, shrubs, and other areas where you don’t necessarily want to blow everything around. A smaller or narrower rake is especially helpful for removing leaves that have collected between plants in the landscape without damaging them.”.

According to recent reports, it’s also important to invest in a good-quality rake; aluminum or plastic rakes are best for most leaf cleanups. Unlike leaf blowers, a durable rake is affordable, easy, and practical to use, and doesn’t need fuel or batteries.

According to recent reports, if in doubt, though, check out these different types of rakes suitable for your yard. For more top tips, check out how to rake leaves the easy way — 7 tips and tricks.

A top tip is to (ideally) rake on a dry day, as the leaves will be easier to gather and less of a chore.

It has been revealed that also, you don’t have to clear every single leaf off your lawn, since keeping a few around can actually benefit your garden plants. “Don’t blow or rake every leaf out of your garden beds just for the sake of making them spotless,” adds Musgrave.

“Some leaf litter can be beneficial for the soil as it breaks down and adds organic matter. It can also provide overwintering habitat for beneficial insects. You don’t want leaves piled so heavily that they smother smaller plants, but a light layer can be left in place.”.

In a recent development, shredding leaves with a lawn mower is another handy trick. Breaking them down into smaller pieces makes it easy to add them to your compost heap and return those valuable nutrients to your yard.

“Excess leaves can also be added to a compost pile rather than bagged and thrown away. Chopping or shredding them first can help them break down more quickly. The key is to make sure the leaves aren’t so thick they cover the grass and block sunlight and air.”.

Sources indicate that finally, pay attention to bare spots and thin areas. Depending on your grass type and climate, consider overseeding before the harsh winter arrives. “Apply a grass seed that is appropriate for your lawn, lightly rake it into the soil, and keep the area consistently moist while the new grass gets established.

Industry observers note that "The cooler temperatures of fall are ideal for establishing grass. Taking care of thin and bare spots now gives latest grass time to develop roots before winter and helps create a fuller, healthier lawn for spring.”.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the tech giant has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its looks to develop autonomous AI agents:.

In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

Recent findings suggest that “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

In a recent development, today’s report on the fresh job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring users to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the tech giant could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the newly introduced job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how rapidly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.
